name: Lyrikai: Fibonacci Protocol for UI/UX Design Agents

vectors.about: Every checked length is a rung, 0, intrinsic, or in its fixed set. Negative rungs pass.
Off-ladder lengths, an off-set radius and an off-set stroke each fail. In a shorthand each value is tested.
At u = 4 the rungs are F × 4 plus the sub-unit values 1 and 2. Radius, stroke and container widths stay in platform units. 13 and 16 are not rungs; 2440 (610 × 4) is not a rung.

The two derived patterns pass: a φ split of a container, and a container minus one ladder token. Rung arithmetic, chaining, a non-rung operand, a non-φ factor, and a literal 987px in place of the container token fail.

Overlay tests resolved values. A host token that resolves to a rung passes; an icon-role token is not tested; a host token that is not a rung fails unless it is a declared exception (addressed by token or by selector). A pending exception makes the run pending when nothing else fails; here .b fails outright.

A 4-based scale at u = 1: nearest rung, ties go up (4 → 5), drift at most 25%, merges listed. Radii map to the radius set; 32 is over 25% from 21 and is not snapped. The values that cannot be snapped are declared as accepted snap-drift exceptions, so the run passes.

The same scale at u = 4: 2 is a sub-unit value and is kept; 6 drifts 33% and is not snapped; 16 is a tie between 12 and 20 and goes up. The values that cannot be snapped are declared as accepted snap-drift exceptions, so the run passes.

Target tokens end at no less than max(original, ladder target) and have no drift limit: 32, 40 and 44 become 55; 64 may stay or become 89. A drawn-role token and an icon-role token are unchanged. Order is kept within a role group only: target 32 → 55 beside spacing 36 → 34 is not a breach.
The same tokens with pointer: fine declared. The ladder target is 34, so 32 becomes 34, 40 and 44 become 55 (the smallest rung at or above the original), and 64 may stay.

Overrides: 16 → 21 (31.3%) passes; 24 → 34 (41.7%) is over 38.2% and fails, so 24 stays at its nearest rung; 20 → 13 (35%) is within the limit but breaks order against 16 → 21, which fails FP-SNAP-05.

Type sizes by formula from body 16. 20 is a step and 21 is not. Micro passes only through its token. A px size, a fixed or missing line height, 1.618 on a heading, and the unused odd step 5 (53) fail.
The same input with type.align: fibonacci. Now 21 is the step and 20 is not.
Contrast on declared pairs, never rounded: #767676 on white passes for text and #777777 does not; #949494 passes at 3:1 and #959595 does not. Ratios are shown truncated to three decimals.
has.motion and has.controls are declared false, but the scope has a transition and a button selector. FP-CONF-11 fails twice: a rule may not be marked n/a when its condition is true.
The same input with has.motion and has.controls declared true. No contradiction.

Overlay: only the scope is tested. Coverage is the checked values in the scope divided by those in the whole source, counted after shorthand expansion (padding: 21px is four values, gap: 8px is two). The legacy file is outside the scope and is not flagged.
The twin of 06-snap-u1 with no exceptions declared. The values that cannot be snapped are kept without a snap-drift exception, which fails FP-SNAP-10.
The twin of 07-snap-u4 with no exceptions declared. The values that cannot be snapped are kept without a snap-drift exception, which fails FP-SNAP-10.
